reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Since August 2026, field manual-read route completion for the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts (E-02); the resulting incomplete/late reads trigger estimate substitution at billing import, producing ESTIMATED-read bills that account for part of the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-01, E-07). Dispute response handling remains within SLA (E-03), so this field-read-coverage degradation — not slow ticket handling — is the best-supported mechanism, though it explains only the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240/3025) of disputed bills, leaving the ACTUAL-read majority (1785/3025) unexplained by current evidence.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Since 2026-08-01, billing import validation rule BV-17 compares raw AMI register values against a 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13); because v4.2-firmware AMI meters (rollout 2026-06) report registers in '0.1 m3' units versus the 'm3' units of older firmware (E-14), this mismatch causes otherwise-normal reads to be flagged high-consumption and rejected at import, driving 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills via estimate substitution (E-12). This explains part of the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-07) but not the larger ACTUAL-read segment (1785/3025, E-01), whose cause is still unestablished.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
